catalog.title: Website
catalog.summary: An open website brief: the model invents the subject, brand, content and visual direction of a complete site.
catalog.requirement: Original concept and identity; substantial real content; responsive layout; working interactions; accessible and fast

catalog.title: Production Site Refresh
catalog.summary: A fixed source: refresh the live Shutterhaus Visuals production site — same doctrine, a generation better, shipped as one self-contained static folder.
catalog.requirement: All five public pages rebuilt; keyboard gallery and scroll frames preserved; zero third-party requests; no build step; content in the markup; WCAG 2.2 AA; verified performance budget

catalog.title: Restaurant Website
catalog.summary: A restaurant or cafe website with a full menu, reservations and a distinctive art direction.
catalog.requirement: Real menu with 30+ items; reservation and order flows with validation; opening-hours logic; strong identity; responsive and accessible

catalog.title: Editorial Website
catalog.summary: A complete editorial publication with a distinctive identity, substantial content and a considered multi-page reading experience.
catalog.requirement: Semantic HTML; sophisticated CSS layout and typography; homepage plus two content pages; responsive navigation; accessible and polished

catalog.title: CSS Interactive Experience
catalog.summary: An original interactive browser experience built with HTML and advanced CSS, without JavaScript.
catalog.requirement: CSS-only interaction and animation; advanced layout and custom properties; responsive states; reduced-motion support; accessible native controls

catalog.title: Design System
catalog.summary: A complete reusable design system with tokens, components, variants and a showcase of the system in use.
catalog.requirement: Semantic HTML and CSS; coherent design tokens; reusable components; interaction states; responsive showcase; accessible component patterns

catalog.title: JavaScript Application
catalog.summary: A complete browser application built with vanilla JavaScript, meaningful workflows and persistent user data.
catalog.requirement: Vanilla JavaScript; real state and data management; multiple views; validation and error handling; persistence; import/export where relevant

catalog.title: Three.js 3D Experience
catalog.summary: An original interactive 3D browser experience built around a real Three.js scene.
catalog.requirement: Three.js rendering; geometry, materials and lighting; camera and scene interaction; animation; responsive controls; performance and WebGL fallback

catalog.title: SVG Drawing Studio
catalog.summary: A browser-based vector drawing studio where users create, select, transform and export real SVG artwork.
catalog.requirement: SVG-first rendering; editable shapes and paths; selection and transforms; fill and stroke controls; undo/redo; SVG export; pointer and keyboard support

catalog.title: Creative Tool
catalog.summary: A professional-grade creative tool in the browser: layered, non-destructive, fast and dense enough for real work.
catalog.requirement: Real file open and export; layered non-destructive workflow with undo/redo; eight or more tools; autosave; smooth zoom and pan on large canvases

catalog.title: Generative Art
catalog.summary: A seeded generative artwork that evolves in real time and is worth watching rather than a screensaver.
catalog.requirement: Deterministic seeding from the URL; three or more scenes or developments; collaborative interaction; high-resolution PNG export; adaptive resolution

catalog.title: Browser Operating System
catalog.summary: A complete desktop operating system in the browser with its own identity, window management and a shared filesystem.
catalog.requirement: Window manager with snap and z-order; persisted shared filesystem; eight or more apps including a terminal and editor; launcher search; persistent settings

catalog.title: Data Story
catalog.summary: An interactive data-driven story built on a generated dataset, told through linked custom visualisations.
catalog.requirement: Four or more hand-built visual forms with linked interaction; a genuine insight with a narrative arc; annotations, tooltips and CSV export; responsive redraw

runs.notes: A monochrome generative-art gallery site: animated hero flow-field canvas, six seeded procedural artworks (ridgelines, harmonograph, moire, halftone bloom, ordered dither, paper weave) with re-run and expand controls, an interactive halftone lab with contrast/gamma/cell/angle/pattern controls and working PNG export, manifesto, colophon and footer. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, zero dependencies, relative paths, works from file:// and GitHub Pages. Known limitations: system font stacks only (no webfont files, to stay dependency-free); artwork appearance varies by seed since every image is generated at run time; canvases require JavaScript.

GRAIN is a fictional monochrome film laboratory website built as a static, dependency-free single-page experience. It includes original SVG artwork, a canvas-based interactive grain simulator, accessible navigation/filter/form behaviors, and responsive editorial layout. Limitations: the contact form is client-side only (no backend submission), the mailto address uses an .example domain, and canvas grain rendering is randomized per adjustment rather than seeded for deterministic frames.

PENUMBRA — a single-page monochrome exhibition of six generative artworks, all drawn at runtime with Canvas 2D from seeded value-noise and an ordered-dither pass; no image files, no external dependencies, no build step. Each work opens into a dialog with live controls (seed, scale, contrast, invert) and PNG export. Includes a keyboard-operable eleven-value grey scale, a scroll-progress rule, scroll reveals, a permanently fixed difference-blend header, and full prefers-reduced-motion, focus-visible, print and noscript fallbacks. Known limitations: the hero dot field animates only while visible and is capped near 30fps, so lower-power devices may drop frames; the serif and grotesque are system-font stacks, so letterforms shift slightly between platforms; the difference-blend header can lose contrast over mid-grey artwork frames.

The Quiet Index: a monochrome editorial field guide to silence with an interactive anechoic-chamber diagram, a seven-entry ledger and a draggable decibel scale. Single static page, no dependencies or external assets. Known limitation: the generated Web Audio tone is intentionally minimal and requires a user gesture.
